illustration.alt: The companion with an umbrella in the rain, a drop on the tip of its nose.

companionLines.bo: Hi {nome}! It's raining. When it rains I get all wet. But today we're going out anyway, with Emma.
companionLines.pilu: Hi {nome}! Did you know every raindrop has been on a long journey? Today we're meeting one.
companionLines.tango: Hi {nome}! Rain! Puddles! Come on, let's jump in!

illustration.alt: Emma at her bedroom window watching the rain beat on the glass; Pietrolino on the windowsill.

screens.text: It's a grey day. Emma looks out of the window: it's raining, and the drops tap on the glass as if they were knocking. "We can't go out today, Pietrolino," she sighs. "Of course we can," he says. "Today we're meeting Drop. A raindrop who's a bit of a rebel."

illustration.alt: Emma in her yellow raincoat and boots, Grandma with an umbrella, by a little runnel in the wood; one drop is jumping against the current.

screens.text: Emma puts on her raincoat and boots. Grandma takes the umbrella. In the wood, a little runnel carries the water towards the drain. But among a thousand identical drops, one is jumping against the current! "Hello! Why are you jumping like that?" asks Emma. "Because I don't want to be wasted!" answers a fresh little voice. "I want to give the flowers a drink!"

companionLines.bo: A drop that talks. And jumps! I couldn't do that, {nome}.
companionLines.pilu: Did you hear, {nome}? Drop doesn't want to end up in the drain. She wants to be useful.
companionLines.tango: A rebel drop! I like her! She jumps like me, right {nome}?

illustration.alt: Emma sitting by the water, thoughtful; next to her, in a thought bubble, an open tap dripping.

screens.text: "Lots of water ends up in pipes," says Drop, "without giving anyone a drink." Emma goes quiet. She thinks about the bathroom tap, when she leaves it running while she brushes her teeth. And about all the rain that falls and runs away.

illustration.alt: Emma looks at Drop on the tip of a leaf; Grandma waits under the umbrella.

screens.text: Drop looks at her from the tip of a leaf. "What about you, Emma? What can you do for us drops?"

dialogue.together: Ask: what can Emma do so as not to waste water? And what could we do at home?

reaction.bo: While you brush your teeth? I'll try too. Let's see what Emma does.
reaction.pilu: A small thing to do every day. Let's see if Emma thinks of it too.
reaction.tango: Click, off! Easy! Let's see what Emma says.

reaction.bo: In a little bucket? What a nice idea. Let's see.
reaction.pilu: That way the rain doesn't run away. Let's see what Emma does.
reaction.tango: Buckets everywhere! Come on, let's watch Emma.

reaction.bo: Flowers get thirsty like me. Let's see what Emma does.
reaction.pilu: That's exactly what Drop wants to do. Let's see.
reaction.tango: Wet flowers, happy flowers! Let's watch Emma.

illustration.alt: Drop jumps from a leaf to a stone and then upwards, until she disappears into a light cloud; Emma follows her with her eyes.

screens.text: "I promise that from today I'll try to use water better," says Emma. "Even one girl can change the river!" cries Drop. And with a hop, plop!, she jumps onto a leaf, then onto a stone, then up and up, until she disappears into a cloud. "Did she really go up there?" "Yes," says Pietrolino. "She'll come back as rain, or dew, or snow."

illustration.alt: Emma and Grandma put a bowl on the balcony to collect rain; next to it, the flowerpots.

screens.text: At home, Emma and Grandma put a bowl on the balcony. "This one's for the rain," says Emma. "Then tomorrow I can give the flowers a drink." Pietrolino smiles from her pocket. "You gave value to a single drop. Every change starts just like that."

companionLines.bo: A bowl for the rain. Tomorrow I'll put one outside too, {nome}. And then water the flowers.
companionLines.pilu: Tonight, when you brush your teeth, try turning off the tap, {nome}. Drop would be happy.
companionLines.tango: Tomorrow I'll look for Drop in every puddle, {nome}! Maybe she's come back down. Bye!
